1.title: Stop! Go!
1.topic: a girl and her mom walk to the shop and cross the street safely: stop at the red light, wait as a cab and a van zip past, look left and right on green, hold hands and step up on the curb (community, safety, colors)
lines: *Jen* and *Mom* | *walk* to the *shop*. ↘
The *light* is *red*. | *Stop*, Jen, *stop*! ↘
A *cab* *zips* *past*. | A *van* *zips* *past*. ↘
It is *green*. | “Is it *safe*?” ↗ | *Look* *left* and *right*. ↘
Jen *holds* Mom's *hand*. | *Step*, *step*, *step*! ↘
*Up* on the *curb*! | “We *did* it!” | Jen *grins*. ↘
1.expression: Say “Stop, Jen, stop!” firm and clear, make “zips past” quick, ask “Is it safe?” with a rising voice, and sound proud on “We did it!”

2.title: Are We There Yet?
2.topic: a boy gets wiggly on the long Thanksgiving car ride to Grandma's house, so the family plays I Spy and counts cows until they pull into Grandma's driveway (family, holidays, travel, patience)
lines: *Nate's* *family* *packed* the *car* | on *Thanksgiving* *morning*. ↘
*Grandma's* *house* was *far* *away*, | so the *trip* was *long*. ↘
*Soon* Nate *wiggled* | and *kicked* his *seat*. | “Are we *there* *yet*?” ↗
“*Not* *yet*,” | *Dad* *laughed*. | “*Let's* *play* I *Spy*!” ↘
Nate *looked* out the *window*. | “I *spy* something *red*!” ↘
“Is it a *truck*?” ↗ | Mom *guessed*. | “*No*! | It's a *barn*!” | Nate *yelled*. ↘
They *played* and *played* | and *counted* *cows* | *all* the *way*. ↘
At *last* they *pulled* into Grandma's *driveway*. | *Grandma* *waved* from the *door*! ↘
sounds: k·f·s 소리 뒤 -ed는 짧은 't': packed '팩트', laughed '래프트'. '팩키드'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
2.expression: Sound restless and whiny on “Are we there yet?” with a big rising voice, let Dad's “Not yet” sound cheerful and laughing, say “I spy something red!” like a fun secret, ask Mom's “Is it a truck?” with a rise, shout “No! It's a barn!” with excitement, and end warm and happy when Grandma waves from the door.

3.title: Wild Turkeys: Not So Slow!
3.topic: surprising facts about wild turkeys: they run about 25 miles an hour, fly in short bursts, sleep high in trees at night, scratch for acorns, seeds and bugs; a tom puffs his feathers, fans his tail and gobbles loud enough to hear a mile away, his bare head skin changes red, white and blue, and baby poults follow their mother the day they hatch (animals, science, nature)
lines: When you *think* of a *turkey*, | do you *picture* a *slow*, *chubby* *bird*? ↗
*Wild* *turkeys* are *not* *slow* at *all*! ↘
They can *run* about *twenty-five* *miles* an *hour*, | as *fast* as a *car* on a *quiet* *street*. ↘
They can *fly*, *too*, | in *short*, *quick* *bursts* | over *fields* and *up* into *trees*. ↘
At *night*, | wild turkeys *sleep* | *high* in the *branches*, | *safe* from *foxes*. ↘
In the *daytime*, | they *scratch* the *ground* | for *acorns*, *seeds*, and *bugs*. ↘
A *male* turkey is *called* a *tom*. | He *puffs* up his *feathers* | and *spreads* his *tail* like a *fan*. ↘
*Then* he *calls*, | “*Gobble*, *gobble*!” | You can *hear* it | up to a *mile* *away*! ↘
The *bare* *skin* on his *head* | can *change* *colors*: | *red*, *white*, and *blue*! ↘
*Baby* turkeys are *called* *poults*. | They can *follow* their *mother* | the *day* they *hatch*. ↘
So the *next* *time* you *see* a *turkey*, | *remember*: | it's a *fast*, *amazing* *bird*! ↘
sounds: '어'를 하면서 혀를 뒤로 말아 'r': turkey '터r키'. '털키'나 '터키'처럼 r을 빼지 않아요.
세 자음을 모음 없이 붙여요: scratch '스크래치'를 '스-크-래치'로 끊지 말고 한 번에!
wild, fly, night, high, white, mile, time
알파벳 이름처럼 '아이': wild '와일드', night '나잇'. 짧은 '이'로 읽지 않아요.
3.expression: Ask the opening question with a teasing, curious rise, then sound surprised and firm on “Wild turkeys are not slow at all!”, read the speed and flying facts with energy, slow down and soften on the nighttime line, make “Gobble, gobble!” loud and funny, say “red, white, and blue!” with a small pause after each color, and end proudly on “a fast, amazing bird!”

4.title: Found: One Muddy Dog
4.topic: a boy finds a shivering lost dog with no tag on the way home from school; he and his mom dry him, check for a microchip at the vet, put up posters and post online, and the next morning a girl named Rosa comes to bring her dog Biscuit home and invites the boy to visit (animals, community, kindness, feelings)
lines: On the *way* *home* from *school*, | *Ari* *heard* a *whimper* | *behind* the *mailboxes*. ↘
A *small* *brown* *dog* | was *shivering* in the *rain*, | his *fur* *caked* with *mud*. ↘
He *wore* a *red* *collar*, | but the *tag* was *gone*. ↘
“*Somebody* must be *missing* you,” | Ari *whispered*, | and the dog *licked* his *hand*. ↘
Ari *carried* him *home* | and *called* for his *mom* | *before* he even *took* off his *boots*. ↘
*Together* they *dried* the dog | with an *old* *towel* | and *gave* him a *bowl* of *water*. ↘
“We *can't* *keep* him,” | Mom *said* *gently*. | “*Let's* *help* him *find* his *way* *home*.” ↘
*First*, they *took* him to the *vet* | to *check* for a *microchip*, | but he *didn't* *have* one. ↘
*Next*, Ari *made* *posters* | with a *photo* and the *words* | “*Found*: *One* *Muddy* *Dog*.” ↘
They *taped* them to *lampposts*, | and Mom *posted* the *photo* | on the *neighborhood* *website*. ↘
*That* *night*, | the dog *slept* by Ari's *bed*, | and Ari *wondered* if *anyone* would *call*. ↘
*Early* the *next* *morning*, | a *voice* on the *phone* *said*, | “I *think* you *found* *Biscuit*! | He *slipped* out of our *yard* | *three* *days* *ago*!” ↘
When a girl named *Rosa* | *came* through the *door*, | Biscuit *raced* to her, | *wagging* his *whole* *body*. ↘
Ari *felt* a *little* *sad* to say *goodbye*, | but *mostly* he felt *proud*. ↘
Rosa *smiled*. | “*Will* you *come* and *visit* him?” ↗ | Ari *nodded* *hard*. ↘
sounds: 입술을 동그랗게 모아 '우'로 시작해요: whimper '윔퍼r', whispered '위스퍼r드'. 'h' 소리는 거의 내지 않아요.
licked는 '릭트', carried는 '캐리드', posted는 '포스티드'. 앞 소리에 따라 -ed가 달라져요.
4.expression: Begin quietly and curiously on “heard a whimper,” whisper “Somebody must be missing you” softly and kindly, let Mom's “We can't keep him” sound gentle but sure, read the steps (first, next) clearly like a plan, sound hopeful and a little nervous on “wondered if anyone would call,” let the caller's voice on the phone sound thrilled, speed up with joy as Biscuit races to Rosa, and end warm on “Will you come and visit him?” with a rising voice.
practice: heard a whimper behind the mailboxes
